questions.prompt: Before you automate a process, what does Anthropic's ticket routing guide tell you to do first?

options.text: Pick the fastest model, then adjust the process to fit what it does well.
options.explanation: The guide starts with the work, not the model. Model choice comes later.

options.text: Understand how the team handles the work today, including edge cases.
options.explanation: Right. The guide says the more you know about how humans handle cases, the better you can work with the model.

options.text: Replace the existing rules first, so the model starts from a clean slate.
options.explanation: The guide asks where the existing rules fail. That tells you what to fix; it doesn't say to remove them first.

questions.prompt: Why break "customer support" into separate tasks before building?

options.text: So you can prompt and test each task on its own.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's support guide and OpenAI's evaluation guide both describe steps you can work on and evaluate one at a time.

options.text: So the whole conversation can be sent to the model as one long prompt.
options.explanation: Neither guide says that. Splitting is about prompting and testing each part on its own, not about prompt length.

questions.prompt: A step's output is "a fair decision", but nobody can describe what makes it fair. What does OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise guide suggest?

options.text: The model will work it out on its own from enough examples of past emails and decisions.
options.explanation: The guide's rule of thumb points the other way: if you can't describe good, the model can't reliably hit it.

options.text: Ask the model to be fair and to explain its reasoning in each reply.
options.explanation: An explanation doesn't help if nobody has said what fair means. The definition has to come first.

options.text: If you can't describe "good" in a sentence or two, the model can't reliably hit it.
options.explanation: Right. Write the rule down first; then the step can be tested.
